Subject: Recap: EdgePath private deployment perf requirements + next steps

Hi Lara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the private/VPC deployment qualification.

Key perf targets you confirmed:
- Interactive UI (token streaming): p50 <= 60 ms, p95 <= 300 ms end-to-end (client -> app -> Redwood -> app -> client).
- Throughput: steady-state ~800 reqs/min for user traffic; up to bursts of ~1,200 reqs/min for batch ingestion windows.
- Concurrency: up to 25 concurrent sessions during peak; streaming connections ~20 concurrent streams per region.
- Streaming: chunked/token streaming required (low-latency partial responses) and we need to keep idle stream reconnection behavior predictable.

Network/path constraints and asks from our side:
1) Preferred connection: VPC Peering (recommended) but we can support site-to-site VPN as fallback. Please confirm whether you prefer peering or VPN.
2) Egress destinations: please share the subnet/IP ranges that will originate calls to Redwood so we can author allowlists.
3) MTU & NAT: let us know if you have jumbo frames or any custom MTU settings; we will validate TLS negotiation + SNI behavior.
4) Test plan: we will need traceroutes, iperf results for sustained bandwidth, and a short sample streaming call to our staging endpoint.

Attachments: I attached a short traceroute output template (network-traceroute-20260813.txt) we typically ask customers to run and return.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- EdgePath: provide gateway IPs, preferred connection type (peering vs VPN), and a brief load profile (you mentioned you had this) — owner: Lara — due Tue 2026-08-18.
- Redwood infra (Rishi): provide required egress IPs + pre-call checklist for netops workshop — owner: Rishi — will share tomorrow.
- Schedule 60-min netops workshop to run the traceroute/iperf and a streaming verification call — propose Thu 2026-08-20 17:00 UTC.

If that all looks right I will schedule the workshop and include a calendar invite with a short pre-call checklist.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi Lara / Hannah — Rishi here (infra). Thanks for the notes — a few technical clarifications and an action checklist so we can scope the netops workshop properly.

Short answers to Lara's questions:
- Streaming: Redwood supports HTTP/2 server-push style streaming and chunked HTTP/1.1 token streaming; we also have a WebSocket-compatible stream shim for legacy clients.
- Connections: we support long-lived TLS sessions and recommend connection reuse (HTTP/2 multiplexing) where possible. We do not require one TCP per logical session — multiplexing reduces handshakes and helps p95 latency.
- Keepalive: we expose configurable TCP/TLS keepalive and idle-timeout controls on the private deployment config.

Network test plan (what we'll run in the workshop):
1) Traceroute from your egress subnets to our egress IPs (please send the target IPs list after this email).
2) iperf3 tests (sustained throughput per stream) to validate per-connection bandwidth and to check for reordering/packet loss at peak.
3) A scripted streaming call to our staging endpoint that returns token-level chunks — we'll measure end-to-end latency and p95 under a synthetic concurrency profile.
4) Verify TLS SNI, ALPN (http/2), and MTU path.

Operational notes:
- Allowlisted egress: I'll attach the set of egress IPs you should permit (required-egress-ips.txt).
- If you choose VPC peering we will use private addresses; please share your VPC CIDRs and peering account info.
- If you use VPN we recommend configuring DPD timers and an MTU >= 1400 to avoid fragmentation for large token payloads.

Schedule: I can host the workshop Thu 2026-08-20 17:00 UTC; if that doesn't work for EdgePath propose two alternatives and we'll pick the best.

I'll include a short pre-call checklist in my next message.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
